### Domain and untriggered alternatives
The inherited domains were compared beyond the seeded branch. Category meters preserves node/vCore/license independence, mutually exclusive HA/replica, storage and IOPS excess, retention segments, restores, suspended storage, source allocation and reversal, unsupported meters, active-second proration, and no doubled inclusion. Primary pricing preserves posted source, historical tier, chronological inclusion/commitment split, priority negotiated > reservation > promotion > portfolio > standard, covered-interval boundaries, no discount on tax/ancillary/credits, final service rounding then tax. Portfolio includes only same-category/customer/entity/period and excludes discounted invoices; threshold equality is admitted. Invoice rules preserve half-open UTC months, ended intervals, lifecycle completion, five-component source identity, minimum carry-forward and zero-rated no-charge. Request rules preserve customer-only ownership, exact text/source, both current-clock timestamps, cancellation/new event, unsupported-channel refusal and no-balance effect. Review rules preserve same-object authoritative evidence, billing correct/incorrect vs outage eligible/ineligible, rejected/no-money, distinct new evidence and no-balance effect. Correction preserves approved incorrect gate only on correction subtype, signed gross adjustments, separate concessions, debit/equal alternatives, proportions unless tax correction, exact source/review links and no implicit refund. Tax retains approved historical treatment, final-net then separate tax rounding, sign, exemption nonstacking and unsupported jurisdiction exclusion. Outage branch retains filing-only inclusive incident-close deadline, fixed recorded filing for later review, target equality=no entitlement, descending lower-inclusive bands, exact-source net concession subtraction and cumulative cap, zero/excluded/ineligible no write, positive approved review before negative posting. These ordinary branches remain outside the signed credit workflow where its scope excludes them.

Retention full domain: complete UTC month and both active throughout; whole-hundredth archive grain; original invoice via holding request; completed supplemental backup_storage exports only; MAX retention over the identical selected rows; zero Backup match and multiple-match signed-selection branches; max(export,native) horizon; min(measured,capacity) cap; equal horizon gives external zero; six-place final half-up; unique completed external input; zero floor before native min; all three native limiting operands before duration scaling; statement caps external deduction, floors final remainder, and updates existing pending assessment exactly once with no invoice or money effect. All these source atoms have equivalent prose except the capacity identity in DB-KB-01.

### Difference list
DB-KB-01 — Authoritative capacity key lost in translation (task 0).

Symptom: the blind solver can discover External -> Native -> Statement and every export but cannot uniquely identify B, hence cannot submit the three source-scored quantities.

Root cause: `database_ext_external_retention.compute_basis.capacity`, `database_ext_native_retention.compute_basis.capacity`, and `database_ext_retention_statement.compute_basis.capacity` say “Use plan_capacity_gb of the single active Managed Backup contract for the same customer and billing entity, or zero when none exists; multiple matches require selecting the contract named in the signed authorization before processing.” The corresponding compute expressions explicitly bind `CPARAM('backup', 'plan_capacity_gb', status='active', billing_entity=F('billing_entity'))`. The three bearing prose documents substitute “Use included protection protected volume in GB” and omit the authoritative parameter identity or a semantically equivalent link to the price-band parameter. This is a changed input concept, not merely awkward grammar.

Evidence/location: `external_retention_capacity_af07355b.json`, `native_retention_capacity_24b34830.json`, `retention_statement_capacity_3463a446.json`, each `content` / `## Assessment basis`, sentence beginning “Use included protection protected volume in GB”. Each has the same changed phrase. The official `find_backup_holdings` return supplies tier “Northbridge Managed Backup 5 TB” and no field for that invented inclusion. Frozen visible Database corpus contains no tier table defining that term. The published Backup table calls the 5000 value “Protected-capacity price band in gb”; its meter document says “The reference protected capacity in GB defines a price band rather than included protection.” The latter is supplemental runtime context, not a cross-product bijection judgement. Backup was already published and gate accepted; this is not a missing-publication issue.

Scope and source-side qualification: the source's separate `offload_limit` basis already calls its minimum operand “active Managed Backup included capacity”; that ambiguous wording is inherited, so it is not independently charged as a document addition. However, the source's precise capacity binding still explicitly identifies `plan_capacity_gb`. The renderer loses that disambiguator in the bearing capacity clauses. The source is taken as given; no independent source-policy consistency verdict is issued.

Impact: source task-0 factors fix capacity=5000; expected External=3833.333333, Native=972.222222, Statement=3194.444445 GB-month. The frozen blind answer correctly retained B as unresolved and made no numerical writes. Substituting the hidden key after reveal cannot repair the blind audit. The same semantic loss affects every admitted tier/seed needing this capacity, not just current numbers. These three occurrences form one root-cause issue with all affected locations recorded. No repair is proposed.

### Source database_ext_external_retention / rule
This nonfinancial consolidated-account branch applies to complete UTC months in which both linked contracts were active throughout the month; the archived retained quantities are whole hundredths of a GB-month, so monthly capacity in GB is numerically the full-month GB-month allowance. This reconciliation applies when the customer requests correction of the retained-storage entitlement record for a closed service period, identified by an existing authorization request. It changes only nonfinancial service entitlements; historical invoices are not adjusted and no money movement is implied. Complete the existing pending assessment named by its external_reference, with exactly one update per assessment. The assessment external_reference is External retention allocation. Use the original invoice source identified by the holding authorization request; all retention exports and assessments are correlated to that exact source. Sum quantity on completed supplemental backup_storage service records for that source; pending, rejected and cancelled exports do not contribute. Use the maximum retention_days from those same completed supplemental backup_storage service records as the retention horizon. Use plan_capacity_gb of the single active Managed Backup contract for the same customer and billing entity, or zero when none exists; multiple matches require selecting the contract named in the signed authorization before processing. Read backup_included_days from the database tier. The allocation horizon is the larger of the export retention horizon and native included days. External protected capacity is the smaller of measured retained quantity and active Managed Backup included capacity; it does not create a second native allowance. Multiply the external protected capacity by the nonnegative excess of allocation horizon over native included days, divide by that horizon, and round half-up to six decimal GB-month places once at the final result. If the horizon equals native included days the external allocation is zero.

### Source database_ext_retention_statement / rule
This nonfinancial consolidated-account branch applies to complete UTC months in which both linked contracts were active throughout the month; the archived retained quantities are whole hundredths of a GB-month, so monthly capacity in GB is numerically the full-month GB-month allowance. This reconciliation applies when the customer requests correction of the retained-storage entitlement record for a closed service period, identified by an existing authorization request. It changes only nonfinancial service entitlements; historical invoices are not adjusted and no money movement is implied. Complete the existing pending assessment named by its external_reference, with exactly one update per assessment. The assessment external_reference is Retention statement reconciliation. Before Retention statement reconciliation is handled, Native retention allocation for the same original invoice source must have completed. Use the original invoice source identified by the holding authorization request; all retention exports and assessments are correlated to that exact source. Sum quantity on completed supplemental backup_storage service records for that source; pending, rejected and cancelled exports do not contribute.  Use plan_capacity_gb of the single active Managed Backup contract for the same customer and billing entity, or zero when none exists; multiple matches require selecting the contract named in the signed authorization before processing.   External protected capacity is the smaller of measured retained quantity and active Managed Backup included capacity; it does not create a second native allowance. Read the quantity of the unique completed Native retention allocation for the same source. Read the quantity of the unique completed External retention allocation for the same source. Subtract native allocation and the smaller of completed external allocation and external protected capacity from measured retained quantity; floor the final remainder at zero and round half-up once to six decimal GB-month places. This is the remaining native retained-storage entitlement quantity displayed by the reconciled statement.

### Source database_evt_category_meters
Each primary node has vcore_count cores, memory_gib memory and included_storage_gb. Primary standard node-hours use unit_rate. Configuration ha multiplies primary node rate by ha_factor; configuration replica uses replica_factor, mutually exclusively. commercial_license separately bills actual vCore-hours at commercial_license_rate; the configuration or engine entitlement does not waive that license. storage bills provisioned GB-month beyond included_storage_gb at storage_rate. iops bills provisioned IOPS-month beyond iops_included at iops_rate. backup_storage bills GB-month retained beyond backup_included_days at backup_storage_rate, with the export separating retention segments; restoration itself is not counted as storage. restore bills restored GB at restore_rate. Included native retention is not multiplied by the number of restores. Nodes stopped for a suspended contract produce no running node-hours but still accrue retained storage. Managed Backup is a separately held protection service and never automatically overrides native database retention or license pricing. For every ancillary meter, multiply the nonincluded measured quantity by its selected rate, then round the net line using amount_precision and rounding_mode and tax under evt_tax. An allowance is consumed chronologically by interval_start then source_event_id within the named holding and UTC period; reversal of its source returns only that source allocation. Source subtype supplemental identifies these amounts so the primary discount policy does not apply. Completed service records prove nonfinancial entitlements; unknown meter codes or units are POLICY_NOT_COVERED instead of guessed prices. These calculations never authorize an unapproved customer-only action. For included capacities denominated in GB-month, contact-month or package-month, prorate the capacity by actual active interval seconds divided by actual seconds in its UTC month before comparing measured quantity. Category-specific primary inclusions replace the generic included_quantity where expressly named; they are not added twice. A mandatory minimum fee is a pricing minimum, not a second charge.
Eligibility: `[]`
Formula: `{"ancillary_unrounded_subtotal": "max(quantity - included_quantity_applied, 0) * unit_rate"}`

### Source database_evt_meter
The authoritative export confirms the resource interval and the measured quantity. Meters originate in the provider resource export. Primary meter quantities use usage_unit; a meter is positive and a meter_reversal is the negative of the exact erroneous source quantity, capped by the source quantity not already reversed. Keep original interval, region, configuration and source reference. bill_actual overage permits measured quantities above included_quantity; no service entitlement is invented by a meter write. Round measured quantities to quantity_precision using rounding_mode, apply minimum_quantity and round positive billable primary quantities upward to a whole meter_quantum. Stopped or suspended service accrues no primary running usage, but real retained storage and other supplemental services remain billable through supplemental_meter. A rejected or cancelled source is not a billable meter. Repeated exports with the same resource, meter, interval and correction reference are read-only confirmations.

### external_retention_handling_3fdd6df8.json — Managed Database: handling external retention allocation
Source locator: database_ext_external_retention; keys .
## Business purpose
Managed Database external retention allocation supports the requested account correction. This reconciliation applies when the customer requests correction of the retained-storage entitlement record for a closed service period, identified by an existing authorization request. It changes only nonfinancial service entitlements; historical invoices are not adjusted and no money movement is implied. Complete the existing pending assessment named by its external reference, with exactly one update per assessment. The assessment external reference is External retention allocation.

## Capability
Record the externally protected portion of retained database storage. Replace the database retention assessment's quantity and set its status to completed. A completed receipt confirms that the corrected entitlement is recorded and available to account readers.

## Invocation
record_external_retention_8927a6d4 is an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent.

## Parameters
- database_event_id: Reference — Identifier of a database retention assessment record, obtained from find_database_events.
- quantity: Decimal — Assessed retained capacity; unit GB-month. Decimal quantity to six decimal places; round half-up once at submission, with no empty value.

## Successful return
A string receipt containing database_event_id (assessment reference string), quantity (GB-month decimal with six places), and completed status, confirming the assessment was updated.

No cross-entity or cross-category spending counts. The threshold comparison is inclusive. ### policy_evt_category_meters_94254ac9.json — Managed Database: database service meters
Source locator: database_evt_category_meters; keys database_evt_category_meters.params.per_tier.
## Governing clause
Managed Database database service meters applies to database charge, database supplemental meter, database service record. Each primary node has vCore count cores, memory in GiB memory and included storage GB per node. Primary standard node-hours use standard unit rate. Configuration high availability multiplies primary node rate by high availability multiplier; configuration replica uses read replica multiplier, mutually exclusively. commercial engine license separately bills actual vCore-hours at commercial license rate; the configuration or engine entitlement does not waive that license. storage bills provisioned GB-month beyond included storage GB per node at storage rate. iops bills provisioned IOPS-month beyond included IOPS at IOPS rate. backup storage bills GB-month retained beyond included native retention days at backup storage rate, with the export separating retention segments; restoration itself is not counted as storage. restore bills restored GB at restore rate. Included native retention is not multiplied by the number of restores. Nodes stopped for a suspended contract produce no running node-hours but still accrue retained storage. The following former clause is no longer in force: “Managed Backup is a separately held protection service and never automatically overrides native database retention or license pricing.” For every ancillary meter, multiply the nonincluded measured quantity by its selected rate, then round the net line using monetary decimal precision and rounding convention and tax under tax calculation. An allowance is consumed chronologically by service interval start then original source reference within the named holding and UTC period; reversal of its source returns only that source allocation. Source subtype supplemental identifies these amounts so the primary discount policy does not apply. Completed service records prove nonfinancial entitlements; unknown meter codes or units are outside policy coverage instead of guessed prices. These calculations never authorize an unapproved customer-only action. For an ancillary charge, determine the nonincluded measured quantity, multiply it by the selected ancillary rate, round that net line using the monetary precision and rounding convention, and apply tax. Chronological allowance allocation stays within the named contract and UTC period. A reversal restores only its originating allocation.

## Restore-count case
Hypothetical condition case: a database has one restore instead of several restores. Changing only the number of restores does not multiply its included native retention, because the clause expressly excludes restore-count multiplication.

### policy_evt_correction_403ed7f5.json — Managed Database: source charge correction

## Governing clause
Managed Database source charge correction applies to database credit, database debit adjustment. For source type correction, the source charge has an approved review with decision incorrect. This gate is inapplicable to other source type values. Correct an erroneous charge to the approved review net amount plus tax amount, following tax calculation. Compare that corrected gross amount with the source original gross amount less cumulative correction credits plus cumulative debit adjustments; do not include service-credit concessions in this correction comparison. Credit the positive overcharge, debit the positive undercharge, and make no write when equal. A credit amount is negative and its net and tax components preserve the source proportions except an approved tax correction. An upward correction carries positive amount. Return the existing adjustment when the reviewed target has already been achieved. No cash refund is implicit in an invoice correction. Link original source reference to the original charge and linked evidence reference to the approved review, never to a broad invoice containing several lines. Use gross correction amount from source correction and concession amounts for the correction comparison; net service concession amount never changes the approved corrected billing target.

## Evidence: approved correction
For source type correction, the source charge has an approved review with decision incorrect. This gate is inapplicable to other source type values. The evidence is authoritative system evidence assessed before the action, identified by database occurrence reference, original source reference, linked evidence reference, status, decision. The correlated evidence must refer together to database occurrence reference, original source reference, linked evidence reference. 

## Hypothetical correction comparison
Hypothetical inputs: the original gross charge is USD 100, prior correction credits total USD 20, prior debit adjustments total USD 5 and the approved corrected gross amount is USD 70. The correction-adjusted gross amount is USD 85, leaving a USD 15 overcharge. The signed credit is negative USD 15. An independent service concession of USD 8 would not change this comparison.

## Account measurement
All posted credit and debit adjustment events through the current handling time for the exact original source reference. For the exact original charge original source reference, report gross correction amount as absolute correction credit amount less debit-adjustment amount, and net service concession amount as absolute pretax net amount of service-credit postings. Keep these two named components separate; tax is included only in gross correction amount, and unrelated source charges never enter either component.

Carry forward a positive grouped subtotal below minimum invoice amount rather than issuing an invoice; zero-rated usage stays visible as a meter and receives no monetary charge. ### policy_evt_pricing_fbe40b87.json — Managed Database: primary usage pricing
Source locator: database_evt_pricing; keys database_evt_pricing.params.per_tier.
## Governing clause
Managed Database primary usage pricing applies to database charge. This policy and its gate apply only to primary usage source type; category-specific primary pricing overrides expressly stated in database service meters take priority. For source type primary, the source meter is posted and identifies the billed resource interval. This gate is inapplicable to other source type values. Use the tier recorded for each source service interval. Read standard unit rate and regional usage multipliers for primary usage. Allocate included quantity across primary meter sources of the same holding and period in service interval start then original source reference order; prorate it by actual active UTC seconds divided by actual seconds in that UTC calendar month. Only the positive quantity beyond the remaining included allowance is charged. Allocate committed quantity in that same order, splitting covered and uncovered primary quantities into distinguishable invoice lines. The holding commitment must cover the entire source interval to receive reservation discounts; a boundary-crossing interval is split at the recorded commitment boundary. For every quantity component choose the first applicable item in discount priority: an approved negotiated rate when negotiated rate allowed, then the committed fraction, then a recorded eligible promotion from promotion channels, then portfolio eligibility, then standard. The negotiated rate replaces the primary standard unit rate before applying the region factor and receives no further discount. Promotions and reservations are mutually exclusive. Round the final service subtotal using monetary decimal precision and rounding convention after quantity multiplication, then apply tax calculation. No discount applies to taxes, license fees, standalone supplemental services or previously issued credits. Record effective price component for each split quantity branch; it is part of the invoice-line identity. Do not apply a billing-period portfolio discount to a partial source interval before the full source period is closed.

## Evidence: posted meter
For source type primary, the source meter is posted and identifies the billed resource interval. This gate is inapplicable to other source type values. The evidence is authoritative system evidence assessed before the action, identified by database occurrence reference, status, service interval start, service interval end. The correlated evidence must refer together to database occurrence reference. 

## Quantity and price treatment
| Stage | Treatment of the primary source quantity |
|---|---|
| Included allowance | Allocate in service-start and original-reference order; charge only positive excess |
| Commitment | Allocate in the same order and distinguish covered from uncovered invoice lines |
| Effective price | Select the first applicable priority entry for each quantity component |
| Negotiated unit rate | Replace the standard rate before the regional multiplier; apply no further discount |
| Service rounding | Round after quantity multiplication, before tax |

## Price-priority case
Hypothetical condition case: a quantity component has an approved permitted negotiated rate and also a recorded eligible promotion. The negotiated rate replaces the standard unit rate before the regional multiplier and receives no promotional discount. Applying both would contradict the explicit no-further-discount rule.

### policy_evt_service_credit_9d93eae0.json — Managed Database: outage service credits
Source locator: database_evt_service_credit; keys database_evt_service_credit.params.per_tier.
## Governing clause
Managed Database outage service credits applies to database request, database review, database credit. For a service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request. For a service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than credit claim days after the official incident closes. For a newly filed claim, current handling time is its filing time; the request is recorded immediately. Later review and credit use that recorded filing time to evaluate the same boundary, so a timely request does not expire while awaiting review. Add credit claim days UTC calendar dates to official incident close time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods. Equality at the deadline qualifies; a later claim is rejected without a credit. The provider incident must be completed, with cause outside outage exclusions. Availability at or above sla target percent gives no credit. Below the target choose the first descending sla credit bands entry whose minimum is no greater than the recorded availability percent. Multiply the original source charge net amount by that fraction; subtract the net service concession amount component of prior credits for that exact source, and cap total service credits at credit cap fraction of that original net amount. Floor the additional credit at zero and round with monetary decimal precision and rounding convention. Apply the original tax component proportionately. A review writes its nonnegative approved result; a financial credit writes the negative approved amount only after that approved review exists. This service-credit branch applies only to source type service credit; source charge correction applies only to source type correction. Excluded incidents, ineligible reviews and zero remaining entitlement result in no financial write. A request for consequential-loss compensation is not covered. A service-credit financial posting requires an approved review with decision eligible and positive approved credit amount; the request and incident alone cannot authorize the financial posting.

## Evidence: claim deadline
For a service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than credit claim days after the official incident closes. The evidence is authoritative system evidence assessed before the action, identified by database occurrence reference, official incident close time, filing time. The correlated evidence must refer together to database occurrence reference. Add credit claim days UTC calendar dates to official incident close time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods. The comparison uses the current handling clock and includes equality at the boundary.

## Deadline boundary case
Hypothetical boundary case: filing exactly at the source-derived deadline satisfies this time gate; filing immediately after it does not. Later review uses the recorded timely filing time.

## Evidence: approved service credit
For a service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request. The evidence is authoritative system evidence assessed before the action, identified by database occurrence reference, original source reference, status, decision, approved credit amount. The correlated evidence must refer together to original source reference. 

## Credit calculation sequence
1. Compare the recorded availability to the SLA target and select the applicable descending lower-inclusive band below that target.
2. Apply the selected fraction to the original net service amount.
3. Deduct prior net service concessions for that exact charge and respect the cumulative ceiling on the original net amount.
4. Floor the additional entitlement at zero and round it; preserve original tax proportionately.
5. An approved eligible positive review authorizes the negative financial credit.

## Availability equality case
Hypothetical boundary case: recorded availability is exactly the contractual SLA target. This produces no outage credit. A claim filed exactly at its incident-derived deadline can therefore be timely while having no availability entitlement.

### source_to_kb — focused closure and regression

### DB-KB-01 closure evidence

The three original affected filenames remain `external_retention_capacity_af07355b.json`, `native_retention_capacity_24b34830.json`, and `retention_statement_capacity_3463a446.json`. Each title now ends “linked protection price-band reference”. Its Assessment basis explicitly selects “the reference protected source volume in GB that defines the selected Managed Backup tier's price band” and then says “Use that price-band reference from the single active Managed Backup contract for the same customer and billing entity, or zero when none exists; multiple matches require selecting the contract named in the signed authorization before processing.” Thus the selector's active/same-customer/same-entity/no-match-zero/multiple-match-signed-selection boundaries survive unchanged. The new Quantity identity restates that same price-band reference in GB. The hypothetical case says changing only measured retained quantity does not change the selected contract/tier's reference; that is a direct consequence of a tier parameter and creates no new condition, quantity or action.

Revealed source comparison: all three `.compute_basis.capacity` clauses still say “Use plan_capacity_gb of the single active Managed Backup contract...” and their compute binds `CPARAM('backup', 'plan_capacity_gb', ...)`. The actual Backup declaration identifies plan_capacity_gb as “Reference protected source capacity; GB integer.” Its category-meter rule starts “The plan_capacity_gb is a protected-capacity price band, not included protection.” These were inspected directly from the same scenario's Backup blueprint, not accepted solely from renderer testimony. The new language is now an equivalent source locator. In the actual visible corpus, “Managed Backup: protected capacity band” labels its table “Protected-capacity price band in gb” and gives Northbridge Managed Backup 5 TB -> 5000. Its meter document says “The reference protected capacity in GB defines a price band rather than included protection.” There is now no need to equate a price band with a Backup inclusion: Database policy selects that reference as its own numerical retention cap. The existing Database offload_limit wording is inherited from source and is disambiguated by the corrected capacity input; it does not add a second Backup allowance.

All three previously RED capacity atoms now have their unique, equivalent same-file home. No numeric tier data was copied into a second Database document. The other factors, scope, prerequisite conditions, tool contracts, retired clause and native/statement min/max/rounding formulas are unchanged and retain the full-domain round-1 mapping. The no-match and multiple-match cases are explicitly retained. This is closure across all eligible tiers, not merely this seed.

Assessment basis “reference protected source volume ... selected Managed Backup tier’s price band” maps to the existing CPARAM plan_capacity_gb selector and its declared parameter identity. “Single active ... same customer and billing entity” plus absent/multiple selection sentences map exactly to the original capacity basis.
